general: Ash and shadow cover the land; no green thing grows here, and the air tastes of sulphur and despair.
The fires of Mount Doom cast an eternal twilight over this cursed plain, where nothing moves but the armies of the Enemy.
Here every stone is black and every road leads deeper into darkness, toward the iron gate and the eye that never sleeps.
The Nazgûl wheel overhead on their fell beasts, and their screams strip the courage from even the hardiest soul.
In Mordor there are no stars; the sky is perpetually veiled by the shadow of a will that reaches across the world.
The Black Gate stands against all hope, iron-wrought and ancient, and before it the armies of darkness wait without number.
To walk in Mordor is to feel the weight of an evil older than memory pressing down upon every thought and every heartbeat.
The plains of Gorgoroth are strewn with the bones of those who were brought here in chains and never left.
Even the shadows here have weight; they cling to you like cold hands and whisper of surrender and easy oblivion.
Mordor does not conquer with armies alone — it conquers with the slow erosion of hope, one grey and sunless day at a time.
The Eye sees all roads into this land and counts every footfall; no spy or hero has crossed these borders without its knowledge.
There is a smell here that no description can capture — the scent of ten thousand years of cruelty baked into the very rock.
Orodruin belches fire and smoke without cease, and its red glow is the only light in this forsaken country.
The towers of Barad-dûr pierce the low cloud like black needles; to look at them is to feel your will become uncertain and small.
sauron: Every chain has a maker and every slave has a master; in Mordor I am both, and the forging was done with great deliberation.
I did not build these walls for defense — I built them to remind every creature within that there is no way out that I do not permit.
The fire of Orodruin is my forge and my altar; in its flame I tempered the one instrument of my absolute sovereignty.
Let them come with their swords and their fellowship and their hope — I have outlasted empires and the bones of their heroes.
This land is my will made manifest: dark, orderly, efficient, and utterly without mercy for the naive or the sentimental.
Power does not corrupt, it reveals; what you see in Mordor is what every will desires when it is finally free of its pleasant deceits.
gandalf: Even here, in the shadow of the dark tower, I can feel the thin thread of a light that the Enemy has never been able to extinguish.
Mordor was not always this way; I remember when Sauron first raised his tower, and the grief of it has not left me since.
The Ring must be destroyed here, where it was made; no other fire is hot enough, no other will is strong enough.
Do not despair — despair is the Enemy's greatest weapon and he would be delighted to see you take it up on his behalf.
I have faced the Balrog in the deep places, and I tell you that Mordor, for all its terror, holds no darkness I have not already passed through.
aragorn: I have stood at the Black Gate before and felt its shadow upon me; it did not break me then, and it will not break me now.
This is the hour we have dreaded and prepared for; let Mordor see the faces of those who will not bend.
The gate may be iron but the will behind it is mortal in its way, and mortal things can be undone.
March with me to the eye of the storm — not because we expect to survive, but because the world requires it of us.
frodo: Every step in this land costs more than the last, and I am not sure I have enough left to pay the final price.
The Ring pulls me here, toward the fire, toward the one place it can be unmade; I can feel it straining in my pocket.
Mordor has no beauty in it, and yet it holds the only thing I need — the end of this.
I can feel the Eye searching for me even now, and I press myself into the shadow of every rock and pray it passes over.
